name: 5gdeploy (NIST)
what_it_is: A TypeScript/Node.js toolkit developed at NIST that generates Docker Compose configurations and startup scripts for emulated 5G networks. It takes a JSON network-definition document (NetDef) and produces fully-configured Compose contexts for interchangeable combinations of 5G Core Control Plane, User Plane, and RAN implementations.
components: netdef: JSON document defining topology, slices, subscribers, and data networks
netdef-compose: CLI that converts a NetDef into a Docker Compose context (config files + compose.sh)
scenario: pre-built NetDef scripts for concrete topologies (cloud/edge, multi-slice, multi-UPF)
trafficgen: subcommands integrated into compose.sh for traffic generation and measurement
compose helpers: TypeScript modules for IP allocation, QoS, bridging, and multi-host placement
docker: custom Docker image build scripts (dn, iperf2, gtp5g, gnbsim, etc.)
protocols: NDN (Named Data Networking, via NDN-DPDK UPF)
measurement: iperf2: UDP/TCP throughput and one-way latency (--trip-times)
iperf3: TCP/UDP throughput with JSON output
OWAMP/TWAMP: one-way and two-way active measurement
nmap: ping scan to count reachable UEs across data networks
linkstat: per-container network interface RX/TX packet counters via 'ip -s link show' and 'ethtool -S'
list-pdu: enumerate established PDU sessions per UE
Prometheus + Grafana: metrics scraping for Open5GS, Open5GCore, eUPF, and process-exporter
configuration: --cp: Control Plane implementation (free5gc | oai | open5gs | phoenix)
--up: User Plane implementation, repeatable with minimatch patterns (free5gc | eupf | ndndpdk | oai | open5gs | phoenix)
--ran: RAN implementation (ueransim | packetrusher | omec-gnbsim | oai | srsran | none)
--ip-space: overall IPv4 address space (minimum /18, up to 64 virtual /24 networks)
--ip-fixed: pin a specific IPv4 address to a network function interface
--set-dscp: alter outer IPv4 DSCP field per flow using 'net|src-pattern|dst-pattern|value' syntax
--set-netem: apply tc-netem parameters per flow using 'net|src-pattern|dst-pattern|netem-args' syntax
sims.tsv: optional file to replace generated SIM card assignments with physical SIM data
fault_injection: --set-netem: injects tc-netem impairments (delay, loss, jitter, reorder, corrupt) on any named network segment between matched containers
--set-dscp: marks packets with specific DSCP values to test QoS-differentiated handling
modes: signaling-only: RAN simulators in registration-only mode without PDU sessions (OMEC-gNBSim, PacketRusher)
PDU session mode: full end-to-end data path with UE data plane (UERANSIM, PacketRusher, OAI, srsRAN)
radio simulator: software-defined radio over-the-air emulation (OAI, srsRAN Project)
RAN-disabled (--ran=none): core-only deployment for connecting physical gNBs
multi-host: distribute network functions across multiple physical/virtual machines via VXLAN
single-host: all network functions on one machine (default)
constraints: Maximum 253 network functions per deployment (one /24 subnet per virtual network, unique host number per NF)
Maximum 64 virtual networks per deployment (minimum /18 overall IP address space)
Only one scenario may run at a time on a host; others must be shut down first
QoS (--set-dscp / --set-netem) is only supported on specific NF implementations: free5GC UPF, Open5GCore gNB+UPF, PacketRusher gNB, UERANSIM gNB
NDN-DPDK UPF supports both NDN and IPv4 traffic but requires DPDK-compatible hardware
Multi-host Prometheus setup requires process-exporter exposed on port 9256 per host; cross-host scraping fails if port is blocked
Not under active development; only occasional maintenance updates expected
docker_services: amf: Access and Mobility Management Function (CP)
ue*: UE simulator containers (one or more, named by SUPI suffix)
dn_<dnn>: Data Network endpoint container (custom 5gdeploy.localhost/dn image)
tg* / tgcs clients+servers: traffic generator containers (iperf2, iperf3, owamp, sockperf, etc.)
notable_absences: No Kubernetes/Helm support — Docker Compose only
No built-in IPv6 UE data plane support (IPv6 routing mode exists at bridge level only)
No GUI or web dashboard for topology definition — NetDef is JSON-only
No automated fault injection scheduling — netem rules are static at compose generation time
No support for 5G SA standalone over-the-air with commercial UEs out of the box
No built-in CI/CD or test orchestration framework
